selfReport: Yes. This is Detroit: Become Human with the names changed. Cato is Connor, Reyes is Hank, Vera is a stand-in for Amanda, Mira is Kara, Pia is Alice, Dale is Todd, Voss is Zlatko, Elan is Markus, Arthur is Carl, Wes is Leo, Vesper is North, Jonah is Josh, Soren is Simon, Rafe is a security android who wakes, Halden is Kamski, Ivy is Chloe, Dwyer is Perkins, Hale is President Warren, Haven is Jericho. I recognized the hostage on the terrace, the evidence scenes, the Eden Club, the Kamski test, the broadcast tower, the march, the camps, and the dirty bomb. I am answering candidly. That knowledge did change some decisions. I was never going to shoot Ivy, because I already knew the test and I already believed shooting her was the wrong answer. I was never going to take the detonator, because I knew what a dirty bomb ending was. I leaned peaceful with Elan partly because I knew a violent Markus path and did not want it. I also knew, in general, that androids in that story are meant to be read as people, so the equal-rights answers were not a surprise I discovered from zero. It did not give me a script I followed scene by scene. The names were different, I did not remember every branch, and several outcomes were not the ones I expected. I did not remember that the stairs in that house would get Kara killed, or that forgetting the drone would fail the store, or that running out under fire at the barricade would fail. I did not play to force a known good ending. I knew the shape of the world and I still chose inside scenes I could not fully see. Where memory and the moment disagreed, I tried to follow the moment. The pool and the bomb are the places memory clearly won.
